analysis: The open flipped the red-futures narrative (Dow/S&P ~-0.2% premarket) into a mixed-green tape: S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.3%, Dow -0.1% at the bell. But the leadership stayed narrow — 49% of S&P components were losing ground pre-open, six of eleven sector ETFs were down, and Friday left fewer than one in four S&P stocks above their 50-day with new lows outnumbering new highs three to one. Versus the 6am brief, three things changed: (1) NVDA hardened from +0.5% premarket to +1% at the bell, building on Friday's new all-time high with the Foxconn record-quarter print behind it; (2) the 10Y round-tripped the morning oil bid back to 5.30% (+2bp), erasing the 6am 5.26% dip — the bond market still prices inflation (Thursday ISM prices-paid 77.9), not the Fed, even as October hike odds collapsed to ~20% from ~71% a week ago; (3) Tesla added a fresh company-specific catalyst with Musk confirming TSMC-Terafab talks. The Vistra DOE announcement is still pending — today's Perry-plant visit is the de-risking event for a two-wire story with no official confirmation yet. Noise to discount: the conflicting webull 'changes in US stocks' readout (conflicts with fresher US-session sources) and premarket automated snapshot moves. No qualifying fresh HN/Reddit threads surfaced this morning; the 5am Qualcomm-Huawei HN thread remains the last substantive community signal.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Mixed open: S&P 500 +0.2% and Nasdaq +0.3% at the bell, Dow -0.1%. The 10Y pushed back above 5.30% (+2bp from Friday's 5.28 close), near Thursday's 24-year high of ~5.35%; WTI fell 1.6% to ~$89.70.
headlines.why_it_matters: Futures were red (-0.2%) into the open and tech carried the tape green — the open flipped the premarket narrative, but breadth was negative underneath (see breadth headline).

headlines.headline: Opening breadth ran negative: six of the eleven SPDR sector ETFs were down premarket, and 245 of the S&P 500's 500 components (49%) were losing ground ahead of the open. Friday left new lows outnumbering new highs 3:1, with fewer than one in four S&P stocks above their 50-day.
headlines.why_it_matters: A green index print on narrow leadership — the open's strength is concentrated in the same big-cap tech that carried Friday, with the average stock still lagging.

headlines.headline: Nvidia +1% at the bell after Friday's new all-time high ($237.88 intraday), on pace for a fourth straight winning session. Foxconn's record September quarter (NT$3.03T / $95.48B, +47% YoY, 'AI-related operations' growing into Q4) backs the bid; the stock broke past a cup-with-handle entry at 234.76, near May's $235.74 closing record.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hard supply-chain print under the record-chase — Foxconn's AI-server revenue is the closest proxy to NVDA's near-term demand, and this is the one megacap story with fresh fundamental backing today.

headlines.headline: CME FedWatch: traders now see a ~19-22% chance of an October rate hike, down from ~64-71% a week ago, after September payrolls came in at 29K vs ~84K expected (August: 162K). A December hike remains largely priced in. FOMC minutes land Wednesday; Fed Governor Waller speaks at the Istanbul Economic Forum this week.
headlines.why_it_matters: The dovish repricing is the tape's macro tailwind — but the 10Y still rose 2bp to 5.30%, so the bond market is pricing inflation, not the Fed; Wednesday's minutes test whether yields keep fading the print.

headlines.headline: Tesla +1% overnight after Elon Musk confirmed on X that TSMC is in talks on his Terafab chip venture: 'Just discussions, but something may come of it.' Friday's +5% to $370.59 was its best day in a month. Morningstar kept its $450 fair value (+21% implied) with a +10% delivery-growth forecast this year; Gene Munster expects +15% delivery growth next year.
headlines.why_it_matters: The one megacap with fresh company news today — a potential manufacturing partner for Musk's terawatt-scale chip ambitions pairs with a delivery beat and Friday's momentum; the Intel angle (INTC -4% on the same story) splits semis.

headlines.headline: Dow movers at the open: Microsoft +0.6% premarket, battling a 517.78 buy point; Coca-Cola +0.6%; Chevron and Amgen -0.8% each. Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF +0.4% at the bell after all seven names advanced Friday.
headlines.why_it_matters: Big-cap tech breadth is the offset to the negative index breadth — Mag 7 strength is what holds the averages green while the other ~490 names lean red.

headlines.headline: Vistra (VST): Energy Secretary Chris Wright is expected to announce the ~$4.2B DOE loan for Perry/Davis-Besse/Beaver Valley uprates today during his visit to the Perry plant in Ohio (Bloomberg broke it, Reuters confirmed via sources Saturday). DOE and Vistra have not officially confirmed.
headlines.why_it_matters: Two-wire sourced but still unconfirmed by the official parties — single-source, unconfirmed: treat as fragile. Today's announcement is the de-risking event; a confirmed loan funds uprates behind Vistra's Meta 433 MW PPA with federal financing.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news. Today is the TXSE debut — units begin trading on the Texas Stock Exchange under the unchanged ticker USAC after NYSE trading ended Oct. 2; unitholders take no action. Venue move, not a business change (Energy Transfer and Sunoco units also debut on TXSE today). Carried: Zacks raised Q3 2026 EPS estimate to $0.21 (Oct 1), Hold rating, FY2026 consensus $1.17; Q2 beat ($0.31 vs $0.28) on $342.15M revenue; $600M 6.75% senior-notes private placement due 2035; director Bradford Whitehurst bought 6,000 shares Aug 21 at $26.10. Main sector read-through: oil softer (WTI $89.70, -1.6%; Brent ~$102).
